title: CBSE CLASS 4 — Environmental Studies | Water Air Soil

subject: cbse4-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a source of fresh water?

options.explanation: Rain is a source of fresh water.
Rivers are sources of fresh water.
Oceans contain salt water, not fresh water.
Ponds are sources of fresh water.

questions.explanation: Oceans contain salt water, not fresh water, while rain, rivers, and ponds typically contain fresh water.
questions.hint: Think about the types of water bodies and their salt content.
questions.subject: cbse4-evs

questions.question: In the water cycle, when water vapor cools and turns into tiny water droplets, this process is called:

options.explanation: Evaporation is the process of water turning into vapor.
Condensation is the cooling of water vapor into droplets.
Precipitation is when water falls as rain, snow, etc.
Collection is the gathering of water in rivers, lakes, etc.

questions.explanation: Condensation is the process where water vapor cools and forms droplets, a key step in the water cycle.
questions.hint: This process occurs when water vapor changes from gas to liquid.
questions.subject: cbse4-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is **not** a natural resource?

questions.question: Which process is responsible for water turning into vapor and rising into the sky?

options.explanation: Condensation is the process where vapor turns into liquid.
Collection refers to water gathering in one place, like in lakes or rivers.
Precipitation is when water falls from the sky as rain, snow, or hail.

questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process where water changes into vapor due to heat from the sun and rises into the atmosphere.
questions.hint: This process involves the change of water from liquid to gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a **soil conservation** method?

questions.question: If a plant needs **500 ml** of water every day, how much water will it need in **one week**?

questions.question: If a plant needs **250 ml of water every day**, how much water will it need in **one week**?
